q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of pasta per kg?
title: Pasta carbon footprint per kg
short: Multiply the durum semolina per kg of pasta by the miller's figure, then add mixing, extrusion and drying energy. Drying is usually the main plant energy use. Divide the plant's energy by kg packed.

ul: Durum wheat semolina or maida by weight.
Water, and vegetables or eggs in some lines.
Mixing and vacuum extrusion through dies.
Pre-drying and final drying in heated chambers.

p: Report per kg of dry pasta. Long cut pasta often dries longer than short cut, so report by shape family where you can.

example.title: Worked example: pasta unit per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 37,700 / 300,000 = 0.126 kg CO2 per kg
Add semolina and packing for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
